summary.short: Establishes the Artificial Intelligence Centre, a non-profit foundation that coordinates AI projects, gives opinions on AI and deepfake use in elections, and runs a special regulatory environment where it may grant permits to disapply certain legal requirements. Applies from 20 March 2025; some tasks from 1 June 2026.
summary.long: The law creates a non-profit foundation, the Artificial Intelligence Centre, registered under the associations and foundations law. Its tasks include promoting AI use in public and private sectors, identifying AI security risks, issuing opinions on AI or deepfake use in pre-election campaigns, election day and parliamentary appointment processes, preparing guidelines, organising datasets for AI training, and organising a special regulatory environment. The centre may run competitions, receive state budget funding, donations and other income, and process personal data for its tasks. Its structure is a council of nine members and a director appointed by the council. Under Article 8, the centre, working with competent institutions, issues administrative acts that grant permission not to apply specified legal requirements for participants. AI development in this environment may not endanger state, public, environmental or economic security, or human health and life. Sanctioned companies and entities linked to Russia or Belarus are excluded, as are companies subject to criminal sanctions in the past five years. Administrative acts can be appealed in court. Article 9 allows the centre to request personal data from national state information systems for AI development, limited to data minimisation, pseudonymisation where possible, named participants and deletion after development. Transitional provisions set the foundation's registration deadline at 31 March 2025 and start the election-opinion task from 1 June 2026. The text includes a 2026 amendment to Article 8 effective 1 June 2026.</parameter>

thresholds.consequence: A company on which criminal-nature sanctions were imposed within the last five years may not take part in the special regulatory environment
thresholds.conditions: Applies jointly with the other exclusion grounds in Art. 8(3) points 1-3 (international or national sanctions; Russian or Belarusian ownership or control)
